bounded_practice: software maintenance, configuration management, release engineering, and incident handover as a learning and design lens only

proposals.falsifier_or_acceptance_gate: Accept only remasters with an explicit caller inventory, compatibility plan, bounded witness, rollback, and no destructive deletion.
proposals.hypothesis: A bounded dependency and caller audit can identify safe additive remasters while preserving historical compatibility and failed evidence.
proposals.null_or_failure_condition: The audit lacks callers, trigger overlap, rollback, or evidence for a proposed merge or deprecation.
proposals.rollback_or_recovery: Keep the prior family-current surface active and retain the proposed remaster as unpromoted.
proposals.title: GHC Family Reflection-Remaster dependency, trigger-collision, caller-compatibility, consolidation, deprecation, rollback, and evidence-credit tribunal

proposals.falsifier_or_acceptance_gate: Every formal row must preserve locality, scaling and ambiguity obligations and keep empirical confirmation false.
proposals.hypothesis: A typed obligation board can distinguish formal causal-perturbation constraints from empirical GMUT support.
proposals.null_or_failure_condition: The board collapses formal distribution-extension obligations into observed physics or omits domains and units.
proposals.rollback_or_recovery: Withdraw the formal adapter and retain the mismatch as a negative.
proposals.title: GMUT Epstein-Glaser causal-factorization, distribution-splitting, scaling-degree, locality, counterterm, renormalization-ambiguity, EFT, unit, and observation-firewall board

proposals.falsifier_or_acceptance_gate: Remain open_gap while real rows, a preregistered likelihood, systematics, and independent review are absent.

proposals.null_or_failure_condition: The adapter ingests no real rows or lacks selection, calibration, covariance, or likelihood evidence.
proposals.rollback_or_recovery: Retain the zero-row refusal and make no likelihood, force, prediction, or confirmation claim.
